blocks.source: Vol IV, Spatial Memory, § Spatial Belief Failure Modes and Map Corruption
blocks.md: The failure modes of spatial memory rarely announce themselves with operating system exceptions or kernel panic logs. When a corrupted pointer or segmentation fault halts a process, the failure is loud and immediate, even if bringing the physical mechanism safely to rest requires dedicated fallback hardware. In contrast, spatial memory failures are quiet and deceptive. The memory subsystem continues publishing well-formed, syntactically valid data structures at high frequency, while the geometric coordinates inside those structures have parted ways with physical reality.

questions.q: The section **Spatial Belief Failure Modes and Map Corruption** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A state estimator alternates a prediction that widens uncertainty with elapsed time and updates that narrow it below every input by inverse-variance fusion, applying each measurement at its capture epoch and replaying out-of-sequence ones.
A metric loop at camera rate keeps geometry current while foundation backbones update semantics on keyframes, and semantics never certify clearance.
Space last seen free stays free only until an unseen agent could have entered it, so occluded free space shrinks at that agent's speed bound and blind crossings need site controls, not memory.

A transform is a belief with its own epoch, so composing a stale camera-to-slot edge with current kinematics yields a pose the arm never occupied, and the lever arm, not clock resolution, sets the error.
